title: Grateful Dead Live at Kongressaal Deutsches Museum on 1972-05-18

ai_review.summary: Near‑perfect soundboard capture of a high‑energy Europe ’72 show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star → Morning Dew and a gem‑like Sing Me Back Home.
ai_review.review: The recording is a generally clean soundboard source with only occasional cuts, muffled moments and bass distortion, but overall it delivers an even, listenable mix. Musically the concert is a high‑octane example of the spring‑72 European tour – tight first‑set work, a standout Dark Star into Morning Dew, and an especially moving Sing Me Back Home, with Pigpen’s organ and Keith’s piano adding extra color.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.4 stars; most comments praise both performance and sound quality, with only a few low‑star complaints about cuts or muffling.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced mix; occasional tape hiss and loss of high‑frequency ambience. Notable issues: cuts at the end of several tunes (Ramble On Rose), a radio broadcast bleed in Morning Dew, bass distortion on many tracks, Ron’s organ low in the mix, and a foreign voice bleed during Sing Me Back Home.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A strong, tight first set that builds into an expansive second set anchored by a marathon Dark Star → Morning Dew; transitions are smooth and the energy stays high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is praised for sweet tone and a manic duel with Keith during Dark Star; overall strong lead playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh delivers lush, “luscious loaves” on Black‑Throated Wind, though some reviewers note occasional bass distortion.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir adds funky wailing in the Dark Star jam and is noted for his energetic vocal contributions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux shines on piano (Tennessee Jed, Chinatown Shuffle) and shares a “face‑off” with Jerry; Ron’s organ is often buried in the mix but still adds texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: The rhythm section is described as tight and solid, contributing to the overall high energy of the performance.
